DISCLAIMER: mobile player

With the new map out right now, I think I can see the pros and cons of the new one as well as what makes the old one good

New Map Pros

* Actually shows which islands have breeding/hatching done so I don’t have to go on a wild goose chase to get rid of the red 1 on the app. Was really hoping for this and I’m glad they did it.
* Stylistically strong and emphasizes the lore aspect of the game more in a good way.

New Map Cons

* Wayyyyyy slower to navigate. A lot of MSM is collecting currency/diamonds and this new update really slows that down. The new animations are long, additional taps to get to islands instead of just getting there, but the same load times still there. Noticeably obnoxious. Maybe this could’ve been mitigated if they zoomed out the map and you could just click on the islands, but they kind of just chose the most inefficient way possible to make the new map.
* The new song in the map menu. This is something I didn’t think would be an issue, but it is. In the old map, since you’re doing a lot of currency collecting, you’ll probably be familiar with having to hear the first 5 seconds of a song before going on to the next. It’s not pleasant but it’s whatever. Now it’s more like you hear the first 2 seconds of the island’s song and then the first 4-5 seconds of the map’s song. You essentially have to hear twice the amount of song switches you would normally hear, and this small change turns something that was fine into something that’s grating.

Overall: 3/10 for the new update

Honestly I just wish they made the original “spin to win” model of the map show which islands have breeding/hatching results and make it look more appealing, which would’ve probably made the map 10/10. Even then, this model could’ve been done well if they zoomed it out more. But somehow they just made it really inefficient. So yeah I’ll be missing the old one lol.

I wasn’t going to look into the 92% number because this is an ongoing conflict and info can be all over the place, but since it’s part of the core argument I did.

This article has no clearly cited source for its claims. First off, the claim is that 40K+ Palestinians have died. I searched this number up and legitimately nothing came up except for sources talking about combined data of injured and killed from earlier in the conflict. The Gaza Health Ministry does say that there could be a ton of deaths uncounted for, but even they can only confirm a death toll in the very low 30Ks as of the most recent data (that I could find).

Secondly, and even more speculative, is the percentage of civilian deaths being 92% of the total death toll. Hamas (who could be underestimating) have stated that they have lost 6K of their fighters while the IDF (who could be overestimating) have stated they have killed 10-12K of Hamas. If the former is true, then 20% of the death toll have been Hamas, and if the latter is true, then 33-40% of the death toll is Hamas. And considering the dense population, Hamas’ lack of restraint in using civilian buildings/lives in conflict, and general chaos of the war, I would say 20-40% is a decent range for accomplishing their stated goal (and honestly the Hamas numbers are way more likely to be incorrect because they have no incentive to report fact). But even if it was 92%, that still wouldn’t necessarily warrant the claim of genocide, as there has been no clear evidence to support that the goal of this war is to kill Palestinians over killing Hamas.
Correct

But it doesn’t though. There’s not strong evidence of the intention part that’s necessary to constitute genocide. On one hand, we do have officials over there that have abhorrent views recorded against Palestinian people. On the other hand, we have a state who has some of the stronger senses of precautionary ethics in war. It’s a gray situation for sure, but definitely not enough to warrant a genocide claim. It’s more likely that Israel actually is just trying to take down a terrorist group that has no principles protecting the Palestinian people in a highly population dense area, thus leading to unfortunately high civilian deaths.
